title: Adopt Task API v2 (task_manager_api) in the Breeze UI
description:
The TypeBuild server (general.typebuild.com) shipped Task API v2 on 2026-06-11. Breeze's task UI is built against the old surface and is missing every management verb. What changed, all live now on the REST API Breeze already authenticates to (Swagger: https://general.typebuild.com/docs; full contract: software/task_manager_api/docs/task-api-v2-spec.md and docs/MCP_TOOLS.md in the small_business_software meta-repo):

1. PATCH /chromeext/{taskid} is now THE management verb: body may carry status (done | partial | cancelled | blocked | open=reopen; server enforces legal transitions, clears claims, records an override submission — mark-done from a UI finally works correctly) and/or priority, assigned_to, group_id, flags, max_attempts, due_at, defer_until, parent_task_id, depends_on. Illegal transitions return 409 with a reason; in_progress and failed cannot be set by hand.
2. New terminal status: cancelled. Default list hides done/failed/partial/cancelled; blocked is always listed.
3. Task structure: parent_task_id (subtasks/containers), depends_on with deps_satisfied + blocked_by on GET task, due_at, defer_until. claim-next ordering is priority DESC, due_at ASC, created_at ASC and skips deferred/dep-blocked/parent-with-open-children.
4. GET /chromeext/tasks now supports filters: status, group_id, assigned_to, claimed_by=me, parent, limit, offset; items include due_at, defer_until, parent_task_id.
5. New endpoints: POST /chromeext/tasks/claim-next; POST /chromeext/tasks/bulk (optional parent + children, max 50); DELETE /chromeext/{taskid} (creator-only); GET /chromeext/users (for assignment dropdowns); GET /chromeext/audit?task_id=&user=&action=&limit= (per-task history); DELETE /chromeext/groups/{gid}/members/{principal} (admin or self-leave, last-admin guarded); GET /chromeext/skill/{id}/versions + POST /chromeext/skill/{id}/revert + DELETE skill; DELETE /chromeext/lesson/{id}.
6. Lessons are now creator-scoped (created_by) — do not assume all lessons are visible to every signed-in user.
7. Claims renew: re-claiming or posting a task note extends the 2h claim TTL — relevant if the UI displays claim expiry.
acceptance_criteria: Breeze task UI exposes the v2 surface: mark done/cancel/reopen, filters, due dates, parent/child + dependency display, assignment via /users, per-task audit history.

title: TypeBuild MCP auth handoff: mint-at-launch token + header injection, mint gates spawn
description:
Eliminate the second sign-in (/mcp authenticate) for embedded Claude Code sessions. Breezefile exchanges its Firebase ID token for an 8h MCP JWT and injects it at launch, so the session starts already authenticated — no MCP install, no OAuth popup, no external browser.

FLOW (per task launch, just-in-time — never mint at sign-in, never persist the MCP JWT):
1. POST https://general.typebuild.com/mcp-token with Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token> → { access_token, expires_in }. CROSS-REPO DEPENDENCY: endpoint tracked in typebuild-claude-browser repo (server code in ~/git_repos/general_flask_app); ~20-line RFC 8693-style exchange, audited, structured errors.
2. Mint success GATES the spawn (this is the failsafe): only then spawn the claude pty. Token is seconds old → 'session starts with expired auth' structurally impossible. Mint call doubles as reachability+identity preflight.
3. Spawn with: claude [task flags] --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <config> where config = {"mcpServers":{"typebuild":{"type":"http","url":"https://general.typebuild.com/mcp","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer ${TYPEBUILD_MCP_TOKEN}"}}}} and TYPEBUILD_MCP_TOKEN set in the pty env (keeps token out of argv — /proc/<pid>/cmdline is world-readable). If env expansion turns out not to apply to --mcp-config files, fall back to a 0600 temp config per launch, deleted after spawn. --strict-mcp-config avoids name collision with the typebuild plugin's header-free .mcp.json while plugin skills/hooks still load.

FAILURE → IN-APP UI (no terminal ever opens):
- Firebase refresh fails → silent re-refresh, then sign-in panel ('Please sign in again')
- network/server down → 'Can't reach TypeBuild right now'
- 403/disabled → 'Your access has changed, contact your admin'

WHY PREFLIGHT IS MANDATORY (verified against Claude Code docs): with a static Authorization header there is NO OAuth fallback — a rejected token = failed MCP server in /mcp, session keeps running, first tool call fails opaquely. Never rely on in-session failure reporting.

DO NOT: put a header (even with ${VAR:-} default) into the shared typebuild plugin's .mcp.json — standalone users need the OAuth flow and header rejection kills it with no fallback.

DONE WHEN: clicking Start on a TypeBuild task opens an already-authenticated claude session with zero auth prompts; every mint-failure mode shows the mapped in-app message with no terminal spawned.
notes: UNBLOCKED 2026-06-10: the cross-repo server dependency is LIVE — POST https://general.typebuild.com/mcp-token deployed (general_flask_app commit ae95303, bead typebuild-claude-browser-iaf closed). Request: Authorization: Bearer <Firebase ID token>, optional JSON body {device_name}. Response: {access_token, token_type, expires_in}. Errors: 401 invalid_request (no bearer), 401 invalid_token (re-run Firebase sign-in), 403 access_denied (account disabled/revoked), all structured JSON. Spec in general_flask_app openapi.yaml (/mcp-token). Also shipped: the plugin SessionStart tripwire (typebuild-plugin) — set TYPEBUILD_MCP_TOKEN in the pty env exactly as this bead specifies and the session self-reports dead auth at start.

title: Interactive run mode: run a task in a new tab with an embedded claude session
description:
New run style alongside the existing headless path: dispatching a task opens a new tab with an embedded terminal (existing Tab.terminal + TerminalSplit + term:spawn PTY stack) and auto-launches claude interactively — the user converses and approves in the tab instead of a fire-and-forget -p run.

DESIGN
- run_style on a task run: headless (current claude -p --output-format stream-json) | interactive. Local tasks opt in (new column or flag); TypeBuild tasks default to interactive.
- Single flags-to-args mapping table (one source of truth in the client): chrome -> --chrome, resume -> --resume, auto -> permissive permission mode (e.g. --permission-mode acceptEdits; MUST NOT bypass the server-side human-gated submit). Replaces the hardcoded --chrome in electron/agents/claude.ts ~106 (fm-m2dq experiment — validated, now generalize). Unknown flags: ignore + warn.
- Local schema: add flags column (JSON array) to tasks table so the task definition is synchronized with the TypeBuild flags vocabulary.
- Initial prompt passed as positional arg to claude (or written to PTY post-spawn — verify cleanest, document choice). Env: BREEZE_TASK_ID, BREEZE_RUN_ID, BREEZE_PTY_ID as today.
- cwd: task folder when present, else home/configured default (folder is optional in the core shape).
- TaskRun row still recorded: running while PTY alive, status from exit code on close. Limitation: no stream.jsonl/conversation_id capture in interactive mode — note in run detail.
- Attention UX: fg-state hooks (fm-z7v) tint the tab and ping when the session goes to waiting — this IS the approval-gate notification.
- Scheduler integration: a cron fire with run_style=interactive opens a tab when the GUI app is running; under headless breezed fall back to headless run or skip + notify (decide per-task or global setting).

title: TypeBuild Start: interactive launch, in-session claim, release-on-exit
description:
Pressing Start (or runNow / cron fire) on a TypeBuild task launches an interactive claude session in a new tab via the generic interactive run mode bead — the user never types a command.

DESIGN
- Launch: interactive run mode with args from the task flags field (server delivers flags on list/get/claim — deployed). Initial prompt kicks the loop, e.g. Run /mcp__typebuild__work and claim task <task-id>.
- Claim semantics (decided): the agent claims IN-SESSION via MCP claim_task. Breezefile does NOT pre-claim over REST — claim is conditional on status=open, so a REST pre-claim would 409 the agents own in-session claim. Breezefile reflects claim state from list polling. If the row shows claimed-by-other, disable Start.
- On PTY exit: refresh the task list (status changed server-side via submit_task); if still claimed by this principal, offer Release (REST POST /chromeext/<id>/release).
- First-ever launch: typebuild MCP server demands OAuth in-session (~8h token) — surface a hint in the terminal toolbar. Distinct from the Firebase REST auth (auth bead); onboarding copy explains both use the same account.
- Claim TTL caveat: 2h lazy expiry — long-idle sessions at the approval gate can lose the claim; attention ping (fg-state waiting) is the mitigation.
- PHI: terminal scrollback contains PHI — no serialize-addon persistence, no scrollback logging for typebuild task terminals.

title: TypeBuildTaskSource: REST provider + TasksPage integration (PHI-safe)
description:
Implement TaskSource over the deployed /chromeext/* REST API (Bearer Firebase ID token) so TypeBuild tasks appear in the existing TasksPage — no separate tab.

LIST/DETAIL
- listTasks: GET /chromeext/tasks?titles=1 (shipped server-side 2026-06-10, audited as with-titles). Poll ~30s + refresh on task-terminal exit. Map to core shape; rawStatus carries failed/partial/blocked; surface priority, attempts/max_attempts, claimed_by, group, flags.
- getTask: GET /chromeext/<id> returns decrypted title/body (PHI) — render from React state only.
- Row actions by capability: Claim/Release (POST /chromeext/<id>/claim|release), Reopen for blocked (POST /chromeext/<id>/reopen). Start is the separate launch bead. 404 means not-visible, render as absent.
- folder: optional; v1 = local non-PHI overlay (task_id -> folder) for cwd hints, possible cross-repo follow-up for a server-side folder/client_meta field.

PHI RULES (non-negotiable)
- phiSensitive capability gates off: active-task sidecar writes (tasks:writeActiveSidecar), title-bearing notifications (scheduler notifyFailure must use task id only for this source), and ANY mirroring into local tasks.db. Titles/bodies in React state only; cleared on sign-out.
- Search/filter over remote tasks happens in memory, never via local SQL.

title: TypeBuild plugin: Firebase auth (sign-in, token lifecycle)
description:
Let the user authenticate to the TypeBuild brain directly from the app — no terminal, no /mcp dance for the REST surface.

- Sign-in UI in the plugin's onboarding/settings panel: email + password against the same Firebase project the server verifies (see typebuild-claude-browser server/app/chromeext_firebase.py). Use the Identity Toolkit REST API (signInWithPassword) with the project's public web API key — no SDK needed in main process.
- Token lifecycle: hold the Firebase ID token (~1h) in main-process memory; persist ONLY the refresh token, encrypted via Electron safeStorage, so sign-in survives restarts; refresh via securetoken.googleapis.com on expiry/401.
- All task API calls go to https://general.typebuild.com/chromeext/* with `Authorization: Bearer <ID token>` (REST path uses Firebase ID tokens directly — distinct from the MCP OAuth path in server/app/mcp_auth.py, which Claude Code handles itself in-terminal).
- Sign-out clears memory + safeStorage. Never log tokens. 401 mid-session → silent refresh, then re-auth prompt.
- Auth state exposed to renderer via plugin IPC (`plugin:typebuild:auth-state`) to gate the task tab.

Note: the embedded Claude Code session authenticates separately (its own ~8h MCP OAuth). First task launch will pop the Firebase OAuth flow in-terminal/browser; onboarding copy must explain the two sign-ins (or note they share the same Firebase account).
notes:
UPDATE 2026-06-10 (UX decision): the 'two sign-ins' caveat in the description is SUPERSEDED by fm-b5at.9 — Breezefile exchanges its Firebase ID token for the MCP JWT at task launch, so ONE in-app sign-in covers both the REST surface and the embedded Claude Code session. No /mcp authenticate, no browser popup, ever.

Sign-in method decision: email/password is the PRIMARY (and only in-app) path. Google sign-in inside an Electron window is blocked by Google (disallowed_useragent in embedded webviews); the workarounds open the system browser, which we explicitly don't want. Ensure every provisioned Firebase user gets a password set (add-a-user runbook in general_flask_app MCP_OPERATOR.md). Google sign-in remains available on the server's standalone /mcp-login page for non-Breezefile users.

Token lifecycle stays as described (ID token ~1h in memory, refresh token in safeStorage, silent refresh). The MCP JWT is NOT part of this bead's lifecycle — it is minted just-in-time per launch in fm-b5at.9 and never persisted.

title: TaskSource provider abstraction: interface, LocalTaskSource, source routing
description:

DESIGN
- Interface: listTasks(filter), getTask(id), createTask/updateTask/deleteTask (presence gated by capabilities), runNow(id, opts), plus change notification.
- Normalized core task shape: id, title, status (+ rawStatus passthrough for source-native states), priority?, folder? (OPTIONAL everywhere — remote tasks may carry it as a cwd hint), flags?, notes?, timestamps.

- IPC: tasks:* handlers route through a source registry instead of calling tasks.* directly. Renderer keeps useTasks() etc.; rows carry their source id.

SCOPE: vertical slice — exactly what LocalTaskSource + TypeBuildTaskSource need. No speculative generic plugin surfaces (verbs/sidebar/tab kinds are NOT part of this anymore).

title: TypeBuild as remote task source: TaskSource providers + interactive runs
description:
Make Breezefile task system multi-source (TaskSource provider abstraction) and ship TypeBuild (typebuild-claude-browser, MCP brain at https://general.typebuild.com) as the first remote source. SUPERSEDES the earlier separate-plugin-tab approach: TypeBuild tasks appear in the existing TasksPage (which already groups by source) rather than a parallel UI.

PILLARS
1. Interactive run mode (generic): running a task can open a new tab with an embedded terminal and auto-launch claude interactively, instead of headless -p. Local tasks can opt in; default for TypeBuild tasks (the human-gated submit requires interactivity). The fg-state hooks (fm-z7v) provide the ping-when-waiting UX.
2. TaskSource provider: normalized core task shape (id, title, status + rawStatus, priority?, folder? OPTIONAL everywhere, flags?, timestamps) + per-source capability flags (canSchedule, canClaim, canEdit, phiSensitive, hasFolder). LocalTaskSource wraps electron/tasks.ts; TypeBuildTaskSource speaks the deployed REST API (flags field + ?titles=1 both shipped server-side 2026-06-10). Formalizes the source? routing already threaded through ipc.ts ~2008-2120.

Synchronized task definition: shared flags vocabulary (chrome/auto/resume, plus interactive client-side) and ONE client-side flags-to-args mapping for spawning claude (replaces the hardcoded --chrome in electron/agents/claude.ts ~106 from the fm-m2dq experiment, which validated the chrome flow). 4. Scheduling: local cron unchanged; remote tasks get a local PHI-free schedule overlay (source, task_id, cron, next_run_at) consumed by the existing scheduler. Interactive cron fires need the GUI app; under headless breezed fall back to headless run or skip+notify.

PHI invariant (non-negotiable, from typebuild CLAUDE.md): decrypted TypeBuild titles/bodies live in renderer/session memory only — never tasks.db, localStorage, logs, notifications, or the active-task sidecar. The phiSensitive capability gates those code paths off structurally.

title: Hooks as source of truth for tab busy/idle + ~15s reconcile poll for missed events
description:
PROBLEM
Tab attention dots (red = idle/needs-you, green = busy) can get stuck RED while a Claude Code session is actively working. Repro: the gai-worktrees/chat-behavior tab showed red while it was provably still generating.

ROOT CAUSE (diagnosed via code reading + Claude Code changelog correlation; see VALIDATION)
Busy/idle is driven by Claude Code hooks via term:fg (src/App.tsx ~L215-247), with a 20s "silence watchdog" (SILENCE_MS, src/App.tsx L187-208) as a safety net for interrupts where the Stop hook never fires (Esc / Ctrl-C / crash / network drop). The watchdog assumes a busy session continuously emits term:data bytes (every byte re-arms the timer at L209-213). That assumption came from the OLD Claude Code TUI which repainted constantly (the code even notes BEL-on-every-redraw at L174-177).

Recent Claude Code releases dramatically reduced PTY output during a turn:
  - 2.1.69  "Improved spinner performance by isolating the 50ms animation loop from the surrounding shell, reducing render and CPU overhead during turns"
  - 2.1.70  "Reduced prompt input re-renders during turns by ~74%"
  - 2.1.84  "Reduced terminal flickering when animated tool progress scrolls above the viewport"
  - 2.1.117 "Fixed idle re-render loop when background tasks are present" (Linux)
  - 2.1.144 reduced spinner animation color count
So a busy session can now go >20s with ZERO bytes (long tool call, extended thinking, slow MCP/web, stalled response) -> watchdog fires -> tab flips to idle (red) even though it is working.

It then STAYS stuck red because:
  1. The watchdog timer deletes itself from the map when it fires (src/App.tsx L199).
  2. onTermData only re-arms `if (silenceTimers.has(id))` (L212) -> now false -> never re-arms.
  3. 'busy' is only re-entered when a hook fires a fresh busy signal (L224), which generally only happens at the START of a new turn. So mid-turn output cannot rescue the dot; it stays red until the next turn boundary.

DESIGN DIRECTION: hooks as source of truth + active reconcile
Stop relying on terminal silence as the primary signal (Claude Code will keep getting quieter). Instead:
  A. Treat Claude Code hooks as authoritative for busy/idle/waiting transitions (already the intent).
  B. Add a periodic reconcile/verification tick (~15s) per live PTY to recover from MISSED hook events (hooks can be dropped on crash, race, or interrupt). User question driving this bead: "since we may miss events, is there a way to verify every 15s or so?"

  Candidate truth-sources for the 15s reconcile (NEED INVESTIGATION, not yet verified):
    1. Transcript JSONL mtime/heartbeat (MOST PROMISING): Claude Code appends to its session transcript (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl) on every model message + tool call, INDEPENDENT of TUI repaint frequency. Stat mtime per session each tick: recent append + no Stop event => busy; Stop present or stale mtime => idle. Needs a reliable session<->ptyId mapping.
    2. Hook-written state file: hook bridge writes {state, ts} to a known path; poller reads + reconciles. Still hook-derived, so gives last-known-state + staleness rather than fully solving missed events.
    3. Process/CPU inspection of the claude/node foreground process (WEAK): claude stays foreground even when idle at the prompt, and server-side thinking shows ~0 local CPU, so it cannot reliably distinguish busy vs waiting. Likely insufficient alone.

  Reconcile semantics: every ~15s, for each live PTY, compute true state from the chosen source and correct the dot if it disagrees with current attention. Heals both stuck-red and stuck-green.

IMMEDIATE PARTIAL FIX (independent of the poll, low risk)
  - In onTermData (src/App.tsx L209-213): on ANY output for a tab whose attention is not idle/bell, flip it back to 'busy' and re-arm the watchdog regardless of silenceTimers.has(id). A quietly-working session then repaints green the instant it emits anything, instead of waiting for the next turn.
  - Lengthen SILENCE_MS (e.g. 60-90s) so the watchdog only catches genuinely dead sessions.

VALIDATION / HOW THIS WAS VERIFIED
  - NOT empirically measured yet. Diagnosis = (1) reading the watchdog + re-arm + busy-re-entry logic in src/App.tsx, and (2) correlating with the Claude Code changelog entries above. Strong hypothesis, not an observed measurement.
  - To confirm empirically: log term:data timestamps per ptyId and capture a >20s gap while the session is provably mid-turn (or instrument the transcript JSONL mtime in parallel and show it advancing during the silent gap).

ACCEPTANCE
  - Hooks remain the primary driver of busy/idle/waiting.
  - A ~15s reconcile tick corrects stuck-red AND stuck-green tabs using an output-frequency-independent truth source (transcript mtime preferred).
  - A long (>20s) tool call / thinking block does NOT cause a false red.
  - Genuinely interrupted/dead sessions still go red within a reasonable window.
  - term:data on a busy tab re-arms + restores busy.

title: pty data stops forwarding to renderer during Claude Code streaming
description:
During an active Claude Code response (active text streaming, TUI redraws, spinner animation), the renderer's fm.onTermData listener receives ZERO events. Confirmed via console.debug instrumentation in src/App.tsx attention monitor: a fresh `:claude` launcher produces 7 [attn] log lines as the shell prompt + Claude banner render, then the console goes silent for the entire duration of an active prompt-and-response cycle, even though xterm.js in the same tab is clearly rendering output to the user.

Symptom user sees: tab attention-tint (fm-4bs / fm-9mh) shows green during initial Claude launch, then stays red forever even while Claude is actively producing tokens. Tested with `QUIET_MS` bumped to 2500 and with the App.tsx subscription rewritten to subscribe-once-on-mount with refs (commit pending) — neither change produced any [attn] logs during streaming, ruling out React-side subscription churn or timer-based flicker.

Where the silence is: somewhere between node-pty's onData callback in electron/ipc.ts (~line 1499 `wc.send('term:data', { id, data })`) and the renderer's ipcRenderer.on('term:data', …) in electron/preload.ts:132. Two paths to investigate:

1. Main-process side: is the pty.onData listener still firing during Claude's streaming? Add a console.log at the wc.send call site (or stdout from main) to confirm. If main-side is silent too, this is a node-pty bug or alt-screen / flow-control issue with how Claude Code drives the tty.

2. IPC forwarding: if main is firing but renderer isn't receiving, the BrowserWindow's webContents may be dropping events under high frequency, or there's a frozen-context issue with the preload subscription.

Also worth checking: does the same silence happen with codex / gemini, or is it Claude-specific? Claude Code uses Ink (a React-for-CLI), which uses alt-screen mode + heavy cursor positioning; either could trip a node-pty path.

Files: electron/ipc.ts (pty + term:data forwarding), electron/preload.ts:128-134 (onTermData bridge), src/App.tsx attention monitor (~line 109).

Diagnostic to add next: temporary stdout log at the wc.send call in main proving whether main-side data is flowing. If it is, the renderer is the culprit; if not, dig into node-pty.

This bug breaks the green attention tint added in fm-4bs and the system notification in fm-c2w, since both depend on attention transitions reaching the renderer.
close_reason: No longer load-bearing. The fm-z7v hook-based busy/idle path bypasses term:data entirely, and the BEL/OSC9 detector that depended on it has been removed (Claude TUI emits BEL on every redraw, which was clobbering busy state). term:data is now used only as the byte stream into xterm.js; that path works fine. Reopen if a future feature needs renderer-side parsing of pty output.

description:

1. PRIMARY: cursor-visibility transition. xterm.js exposes the DECTCEM state (CSI ?25l hides, ?25h shows). 2. BEL (\x07) — xterm onBell event. Instant explicit signal.

3. OSC 9 / OSC 777 — explicit notification escape sequences.

4. Activity-stopped — fallback for tools that don't manage cursor. State machine: IDLE→ACTIVE when bytes_in_500ms > threshold; ACTIVE→QUIET when no bytes for >800ms; QUIET→ATTENTION. Tunable per launcher.

5. User regex override per launcher.

OR all signals. Three tab states: IDLE (nothing), GENERATING (subtle spinner dot, no badge), ATTENTION (pulsing accent-color dot + badge). User typing into terminal clears attention. Visiting the tab clears attention.

title: DSL parser & evaluator (predicates over file metadata)
description:

Atoms: name, ext, path, parent, depth, size, mtime, ctime, atime, birthtime, is_dir, is_symlink, is_hidden, mime
Operators: = != > < >= <= ~ !~ in glob between
Combinators: and, or, not, parens
Literals with units: 1MB, 1.5GB, 7d, 2h, now, now-30d, ISO dates
Tag self-reference: tag:name as a predicate atom (resolves to other tag's match set)

Output: parse(string) → AST; evaluate(AST, fileRow) → bool. Unit tested in isolation, no fs dependencies in the evaluator itself.

Defer: git_status, owner/mode, content hashing.

title: Render-time tag evaluator + row visualization
description:
On directory load, evaluate every live tag's selector against the visible file rows. Compute per-row tag membership in memory; do not persist a match index.

- Row tint by highest-precedence tag (precedence = user-defined order, default = creation order)
- Badge column: stacked colored dots/chips for all tags on the row
- Hover/inspect: show which tag(s) matched and which clause of each selector hit

title: Perf: stop FileRow from re-rendering on every store change
description: Every FileRow calls useStore() via React Context, so any state change (selection moving, mark toggling, filter typing) re-renders EVERY row in the current folder. Fix by making row-level rendering not subscribe to the whole store. Options: (a) split the store context into stable (handlers/dispatch) + volatile (state) and subscribe granularly via useSyncExternalStore with selectors; (b) hoist store access out of FileRow to FolderList and pass only the needed props (selected, marked, yanked, tag) which are already props; wrap FileRow in React.memo with default shallow compare; use useCallback for handler props in FolderList. Option (b) is more surgical. Verify by scrolling through Downloads with held arrow key — should feel instant. Profile in React DevTools if unsure.

title: Mockup adoption — design tokens, typography, Dawn+Dusk themes, grain, ornaments
description:
## Goal
Port the foundation of the themes.html mockup into the app. Everything else (FileRow restyle, sidebar, preview, titlebar, statusbar) depends on these tokens.

## Owns (only this bead should modify these)
- `src/styles/tokens.css`
- `src/styles/base.css`
- `src/styles/ornaments.css` (new)
- `index.html` (font preconnect + link)

## Do NOT touch
- Any `src/components/*.{tsx,css}` files
- `src/App.tsx` / `src/App.css`

## Changes

### 1. Typography
Mockup uses:
- `Fraunces` (serif editorial) — for folder titles, preview H2, row names, captions
- `Inter Tight` (body sans) — for everything else
- `JetBrains Mono` (kbd hints)

App currently has Inter only. Add Google Fonts link (preconnect + stylesheet). Expose `--font-serif`, keep `--font-sans` (switch to Inter Tight), keep `--font-mono`.

Mockup line reference: themes.html:6–8 (preconnect + font link), :129–131 (body + .serif + .mono rules).

### 2. Dawn + Dusk themes
Copy the CSS var blocks for `[data-theme="dawn"]` and `[data-theme="dusk"]` from themes.html (lines ~109–122 dusk, and dawn block added in the iteration).

Variables to include for each:
`--bg, --bg-2, --panel, --panel-2, --ink, --ink-2, --muted, --rule, --rule-soft, --accent, --accent-2, --accent-soft, --hi, --chip, --hero-tint, --grain-r, --grain-g, --grain-b, --accent-ink`

Invariant: `--bg` (canvas) is noticeably darker than `--panel` (chrome) → framed feel.

### 3. Paper grain texture
Copy the `body::before` rule (themes.html:134–138) — SVG fractal-noise data URI, `mix-blend-mode: multiply` default. Override for dusk with `screen` and lower opacity (line ~140).

The grain tint uses `--grain-r/g/b` in the feColorMatrix — keep them wired so the noise takes the theme ink hue.

### 4. Ornaments (new file: `src/styles/ornaments.css`)
Port these helpers from themes.html so components can reuse them without duplicating CSS:
- `.ornament` — thin-rule with centered fleuron (themes.html:219–221)
- `.mini-rule` — short rule flanking a fleuron (themes.html:261–263)
- `.crest` — bottom-of-sidebar ornamental `❦` (themes.html:191)
- kbd styling (themes.html:280)
- `font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums tabular-nums` utility class (name it `.tnum-oldstyle`)

### 5. Theme switch transition
Body rule adds `transition: background-color 240ms ease, color 240ms ease` so theme changes fade instead of snap.

## Done when
- Selecting `[data-theme="dawn"]` and `[data-theme="dusk"]` on `<html>` swaps the palette correctly.
- Fraunces renders on any element with `.serif` / `font-family: var(--font-serif)`.
- kbd tags render styled.
- Build passes: `npm run build`.
- No visible regression in miller columns view (tokens are additive).

## Mockup reference
`design-assets/inspirations/themes.html` — read the `<style>` block end-to-end. Lines ~10–281 are the styles.

Added grain plate + serif/mono utilities + 240ms theme transition in base.css. New ornaments.css with .ornament/.mini-rule/.crest/kbd/.tnum-oldstyle. Google Fonts link wired (fm-f2y will self-host). title: Mockup adoption — layout decision (miller vs single-list + preview)
description:
## Goal
Decide the top-level layout for v1 before the team starts porting the themes.html mockup.

## The choice
The mockup at `design-assets/inspirations/themes.html` uses a single-list + right-side preview panel (3-column: sidebar · main · preview). The current app uses miller columns (n-column cascade, ranger-style).

Three options:
1. **Replace miller with single-list + preview** — closest to mockup, more editorial, loses ranger breadth.
2. **Keep miller, add a preview pane on the right** — best of both; needs proportions work because mockup assumes single list.
3. **Layout mode toggle** — per-tab or user preference; adds state.

## Why this blocks other beads
`mockup-shell` scaffolds the grid-template-areas for App.tsx. It needs to know whether `main` is single-list or miller, and whether `preview` is always visible or conditional. The sidebar and preview beads can proceed in parallel only once the shell is set.

## Output
Write the decision in `design-decisions/001-layout-choice.md` (create if not present). Include: choice, one-line rationale, and any proportions (sidebar width, preview width, breakpoints for hiding the preview).

## Done when
- Decision file exists and is checked in.
- Issue closed with the chosen option (1/2/3) in the close reason.

## Not in scope
- Implementation. This bead is a decision-only spike.

## Mockup reference
`design-assets/inspirations/themes.html` — observe `.app` grid (lines ~142), `.main` (line ~194), `.preview` (line ~245).
notes:
## Decision: Option 2 — Miller in `main`, preview slot scaffolded but collapsed in v1

Adopt the mockup's 3-column shell (sidebar · main · preview + title/status bars), but keep MillerColumns as the `main` content. The `preview` slot is reserved in grid-template-areas and sized to 0 in v1, so we don't re-plumb the grid when file-content preview is un-deferred post-v1.

### Rationale
- **Miller is the product.** Ranger-style N-column cascade is what this project was started for; single-list + preview (Option 1) discards the core affordance for an editorial look we can achieve with chrome/typography alone. Miller's "next column peeks into the selected dir" already doubles as a directory preview — free.
- **v1 explicitly defers content preview.** Shipping a dedicated preview pane now (Option 1) means designing around an empty pane. Option 2 lets us ship the mockup's chrome immediately and light the pane up later by flipping one CSS var.
- **No layout toggle yet (Option 3).** Adds per-tab state and two code paths before we know we want both. Revisit after the preview pane actually lands.

### Implications for fm-dxl (shell scaffold)
- **grid-template-columns:** `var(--sidebar-w, 240px) 1fr var(--preview-w, 0)` — preview collapsed in v1; flip `--preview-w: 360px` (mockup value) when the pane ships.
- **grid-template-rows:** `48px auto 1fr 24px` (title · tabs+pathbar · main · status).
- **grid-template-areas:**
  `"title title title" / "chrome chrome chrome" / "side main preview" / "status status status"`
- **Named slots:** `title`, `chrome` (Tabbar+Pathbar), `side`, `main` (MillerColumns unchanged), `preview` (empty `<aside>` in v1), `status`. Sidebar/statusbar/titlebar beads unblock in parallel.
- **Breakpoint:** < 960px → `--sidebar-w: 48px` (icon rail). Preview hidden regardless in v1.
- The existing in-miller "preview column" (transient peek at selected dir) stays inside `main`; it is NOT the reserved `preview` slot.
close_reason: Option 2: keep miller in main; scaffold sidebar+preview slots per mockup but collapse preview (--preview-w: 0) in v1 since content preview is deferred. Unblocks fm-dxl with concrete grid-template-areas (title/chrome/side main preview/status) and named slots.

title: TypeBuild tasks render empty when tasks:list per-source fetch fails silently
description: The tasks:list IPC aggregation (electron/ipc.ts) swallowed any per-source listTasks() throw into a console.warn in the MAIN-process log. When TypeBuildTaskSource.listTasks() failed on a per-call fetch (transient 5xx / token blip), its entire contribution dropped to zero with NO error visible in the renderer DevTools console — surfacing to the user as a silently-empty task list, even though the background poll (?titles=1&all=1) was succeeding (confirmed via server audit log showing 6 tasks returned per poll). Root cause: the IPC list path is independent of the poll path; a failure on it is invisible. Fix: (1) listTasks() now falls back to the poll-maintained in-memory cache on fetch failure instead of throwing (degrade gracefully, only throw on cold cache); (2) ipc.ts surfaces per-source failures at error-level AND broadcasts a tasks:sourceError event to all renderer consoles via a new onTaskSourceError preload binding.

title: MCP session-expiry clock: in-app warning before 8h token expiry, one-click resume relaunch
description:
The MCP JWT lives 8h and cannot be refreshed mid-session (static header, no OAuth fallback) — a session outliving its token loses the MCP connection with an opaque in-terminal error. Breezefile minted the token, so it knows the exact expiry timestamp: use it.

- Track expires_in from the mint response per running session; persist nothing (timestamp in main-process memory alongside session state).
- T-15min: in-app warning on the session tab ('This task session expires soon').
- At/after expiry (or on wake-from-sleep past expiry): prompt 'Your secure session expired — restart task?' with ONE-CLICK relaunch: mint a fresh token (same preflight path as the launch bead) and respawn with the resume flag (server-side flags vocabulary chrome/auto/resume shipped 2026-06-10, typebuild-claude-browser-f2h) so the conversation continues where it left off. Session is retired gracefully, never just dies on the user.
- Edge: detect system sleep/resume and re-evaluate the clock immediately (timers don't fire during sleep).

Non-technical-user bar: the user never sees a raw MCP connection error; the worst case is one friendly button.

DONE WHEN: a session running past token expiry produces the in-app prompt and one-click relaunch resumes the same conversation with a fresh token.

title: Windows: path-separator normalization at IPC boundary + drive-root handling
description:
Biggest Windows porting item: ~66 POSIX path assumptions (split('/'), startsWith('/'), === '/') across 15+ renderer files (Pathbar, FileRow, FolderList, actions.ts, dragState.ts, OpenWithDialog, Preview, Terminal, ChipPrompt, etc.). Windows paths are C:\Users\... with drive roots instead of a single / root.

Cheap mitigation: normalize ALL paths to forward slashes at the IPC boundary — main process converts \ to / on the way out, and Node's fs on Windows happily accepts C:/Users/vivek/file.txt, so the renderer stays POSIX-style and most of the 66 sites keep working unchanged.

Remaining real work after normalization:
- Root handling: '/' vs 'C:/' (parent-of computation, breadcrumb root, 'is root?' checks)
- Drive enumeration for the sidebar (list C:, D:, ... — pairs with externalVolumes capability)
- expandHome (~) already uses os.homedir() (ipc.ts:69) — fine as-is
- UNC paths (//server/share): decide punt-or-support; at minimum don't crash

Needs hands-on testing on a real Windows machine/VM — CI can build but can't verify path UX.

title: breeze open from a remote ssh session opens in the local app (reverse path translation)
description:
From an ssh session on a remote host (e.g. vivekhp) `breeze open <file>.md` cannot open the file in the laptop's running Breeze app. Two blockers today:

1. The breeze CLI isn't reachable on the remote — the `breeze` shim is a symlink in the laptop's ~/.local/bin and isn't on the remote's PATH; the remote has no ~/.breezefile/api.json and no BREEZE_API_* env, so even an installed CLI can't find the app (bin/breeze.mjs:75-89, apiStrict notRunning at :134-136).
2. Path mismatch. cmdOpen sends the remote's ABSOLUTE path (resolveOpenPath, bin/breeze.mjs:633-654). The comment there assumes the app has a *matching* sshfs view at the same abs path. That holds for the original remote-attach direction (CLI on remote -> app on remote-mounted-on-laptop at identical paths), but NOT for the common case here: the laptop sshfs-mounts the remote at /home/vivek/vivekhp, so remote /home/vivek/foo.md must be rewritten to /home/vivek/vivekhp/foo.md before the laptop app (api-server.ts:153 /app/open) can read it.
design:
Reuse the existing source/mount registry. dcd57df already maps 'folder under a connected sshfs mount <-> remote path' for task auto-route-by-folder (electron/sources.ts). This bead needs the INVERSE mapping (remote abs path -> laptop's local sshfs mount path) applied to /app/open.

Pieces to wire:
- Reachability: install/expose breeze on the remote and export BREEZE_API_HOST/PORT/TOKEN into the ssh session (forward tunnel back to the laptop app), or have the laptop app push these when a host is connected. Ties into the breezed connected-hosts work (P4) and the no-terminal-pane attach UX (see feedback-remote-attach-ux memory).
- Path translation: when the app receives /app/open with a path that lives on a connected remote source, rewrite to the local mount before classify+open. Alternatively translate CLI-side using the source registry.

title: Sidebar Active Tasks doesn't refresh on status→done via API/CLI
description:
Symptom: creating a task via the breeze CLI (HTTP → api-server → tasks.createTask) updates the sidebar Active Tasks live. - broadcastChange fires but the renderer's tasksList query hits a stale snapshot (better-sqlite3 should be synchronous — verify)
- 'tasks:changed' is being delivered but useTasks's setTasks call is being suppressed because the array reference looks stale

- The api-server's import path ends up with a different module instance of tasks.ts than the IPC handler (would be a build/bundling bug — check vite/electron config)
- Some debounce/batch on the renderer side

Repro:
1. App running. Sidebar shows pending task X.
2. From CLI: breeze done <X>
3. Sidebar still lists X. ⌘R to refresh — X gone.

Source pointers:
- electron/tasks.ts:440 updateTask, :531 broadcastChange call, :564 broadcastChange impl
- electron/api-server.ts:199 PATCH /tasks/:id route
- src/tasks.ts:43 onTasksChanged subscription, :31 fm.tasksList re-pull
- src/components/Sidebar.tsx:430 ActiveTasksSection useTasks({})

Start by adding a console.log in the renderer's tasks:changed handler and one in broadcastChange. Confirm both fire; if both fire, the bug is downstream in the reload/filter; if only create fires, it's in the broadcast path.

title: Rebind orphaned ptys after renderer reload (lost attention dot)
description:
Bug: after a renderer reload (Vite HMR full-reload, store-shape change, dev restart, or window reload), the main-process ptys stay alive but the renderer loses tab.terminal because tabs aren't persisted (store.tsx ~556-567). Result: Claude Code Stop hooks POST {pty_id, state:'idle'} to /claude-state; api-server fires term:fg via dispatchTerminalFg; App.tsx:154 findIndex returns -1 because no tab in the rebuilt state has terminal.ptyId === that id; dispatch silently no-ops; the green→red attention dot never appears.

Repro:
1. Open a tab, run :term, run :claude (or any AI launcher) — note BREEZE_PTY_ID baked into the pty env.
2. Trigger a renderer reload (edit a persisted-state shape in store.tsx, or hard-reload the window).
3. Tab strip rebuilds with a fresh tab and no terminal pane.
4. Claude finishes its turn — Stop hook POSTs idle. Nothing flips red.

Fix options:
- (A) Persist a minimal {ptyId, cwd, label} in localStorage as part of each Tab; on mount, ask main 'is pty N alive?' and re-attach if so.
- (B) On mount, ask main for the list of live ptys owned by this webContents and reconcile to tabs by cwd.

Prefer (A) — simpler, deterministic, handles the case where there's no surviving tab to reconcile against. Need to think about: stale ids surviving an Electron-main restart (pty ids reset to 0); show a 'pty closed' marker in that case rather than silently restoring a dead reference.

title: CLI fallback when Breeze is not running: direct SQLite reads + write journal
description:
The CLI must work even if the Breeze GUI is closed. Capture flows depend on `breeze task add "..."` never failing.

On every CLI invocation:
1. Try HTTP (api.json present and port open). If success, use it. Done.
2. If HTTP fails (no api.json, ECONNREFUSED, stale PID), fall back:
   - READS (list, show): open ~/.breezefile/tasks.db directly via better-sqlite3 in read-only mode. Same schema. Return results normally.
   - WRITES (add, edit, done, pin, delete): append a JSON line to ~/.breezefile/pending.jsonl describing the operation. CLI exits 0 with a hint like "queued; will sync when Breeze launches".
3. On Breeze launch, drain pending.jsonl: replay each operation through the same code path the IPC handlers use. Move the file to pending.applied.<timestamp>.jsonl on success (keep one rotation for debugging). Best-effort; if a write fails (e.g. id already deleted), log and skip.

Operation `breeze task open <id>` requires the GUI; in fallback mode it should `open -a Breeze` (launch the app) and queue a navigation intent for the app to consume on startup.

Concurrency: WAL mode on the SQLite db so direct reads do not block app writes. Document this clearly.

title: External API: CLI + local HTTP for AI CLIs and scripts to interact with tasks
description:
Expose the task system to external tools so Claude Code, scripts, and shortcuts can create/list/update tasks without going through the Breeze UI.

Architecture (proposed, refine in design):

1. LOCAL HTTP SERVER in Electron main process. Bound to 127.0.0.1 on a random port chosen at startup. Port + bearer token written to ~/.breezefile/api.json (mode 600). RESTful endpoints mirror the existing tasks IPC handlers:
   GET    /tasks?status=&folder=
   POST   /tasks            (create)
   PATCH  /tasks/:id        (update)
   DELETE /tasks/:id
   GET    /tasks/:id

2. BREEZE CLI — a thin Node script installed via the same Homebrew tap. Reads ~/.breezefile/api.json, talks to the HTTP server. Subcommands:
   breeze task add "Fix bug" --folder . --due 2026-05-01
   breeze task list --status=pending --json
   breeze task done <id>
   breeze task open <id>      # navigate Breeze tab to folder

3. AUTH: bearer token regenerated on app start, written to api.json. Anyone with read access to that file can call the API; that is fine because they already have read access to ~/.breezefile/tasks.db.

4. WHEN BREEZE IS NOT RUNNING: CLI falls back to direct SQLite (better-sqlite3) for reads, queues writes in a journal file that the app drains on next launch. Keeps capture flows working in any shell, anytime.

5. MCP SERVER (later): wrap the same surface as MCP tools so Claude/Codex/Gemini can call them natively without shelling out. Build only once HTTP+CLI prove the model.

6. SECURITY: localhost-only bind, token check on every request, no CORS for browser, basic rate-limit.

Unlocks select-tasks-and-do-with-claude workflows: claude can shell out to breeze task list --in-progress to know what to work on, and breeze task done <id> when finishing.

// icons.tsx exports a symbol sprite mounted once at app root.
export function IconSprite(): JSX.Element { /* the inline <svg> with <defs> */ }

title: Notifications when start_at arrives (and optional near-due reminders)
description:
On Breeze startup and once daily (e.g. 8am local), check for tasks where start_at = today and not yet seen. Show a native macOS notification grouping them ('3 tasks starting today: …'). User opens Breeze to see them.

Optional: same daily check for tasks due tomorrow (configurable in Settings: off / start-only / start+near-due). Default: start-only.

Track 'last_notified_for_date' per task to avoid re-firing within the same day. Settings toggle to disable globally.

Must survive across app restarts — store last-checked date in app prefs.

title: Export tasks (JSON) + Import; basic backup story
description:
Settings action: 'Export tasks' writes JSON of all tasks to a user-chosen location. 'Import tasks' reads a JSON file and merges (by id; collisions prompt overwrite-or-skip).

Motivation: ~/.breezefile/tasks.db is local-only, not synced. Power users may want to back up to Drive/Dropbox manually, or move between machines. JSON is the lingua franca.

Schema for export: array of task objects matching the SQL columns, plus a top-level {version, exported_at} envelope so future migrations can reshape. Keep simple; this is for users, not for replication.

title: [later] Multi-split / quad-pane terminal layout in a tab
description: Once single-split feel is right, allow multiple terminal splits in a tab — vertical/horizontal/quad. Build a split-pane primitive (react-mosaic or hand-rolled flex splits) where each leaf is a folder pane or terminal pane. Drag-to-resize. Each terminal independently named/themed/attention-tracked. Tab-level attention is OR of all panes.

title: Phase 2: LLM-suggested tag name + color
description:
When LLM emits a selector, also propose:
- A short tag name (kebab-case, <20 chars)
- A color from the existing palette (semantic match: red for cleanup/danger, blue for work, green for archive, etc.)

User can override before saving. Small polish but raises perceived intelligence significantly.

title: Frozen tag mode (snapshot of paths)
description:
Variant of live tags: at save time, snapshot the set of matching paths into the tag's 'snapshot' field. Subsequent visualization uses the snapshot, not re-evaluation.

Use case: 'the 247 files I tagged at 3pm yesterday' — stable target for cleanup reviews.

UX: toggle on the tag-input modal; 're-snapshot' action available from tag detail view.

description: Expose OpenWithDialog through a chip-prompt verb 'open-with'. Verb opens the existing dialog prefilled with cursor/selection. Keeps the dialog as single source of truth; verb is just a discovery surface alongside context menu.

title: Mockup adoption — paper grain background
description: Subtle SVG fractal-noise tile applied as a fixed full-window background via multiply blend (light themes) / screen blend (dusk). Tint derived from theme tokens. Implemented once in global CSS; grain color adjusts per data-theme. Visually load-bearing — kills the flat feel.
close_reason: Grain from fm-19e was mounted on body::before but hidden by opaque .app bg, and its feColorMatrix ignored --grain-r/g/b. Rewired grain onto chrome surfaces only (titlebar/tabbar/pathbar/modeline/statusbar), with per-theme tint via SVG-alpha-mask + CSS bg-color reading --grain-r/g/b. Main pane stays grain-free as the recessed plate. Dusk/feminism-night use screen blend.

title: Mockup adoption — framed-luminance invariant on main pane
description: Main content pane visually recesses: --bg (center) ~10-14% darker than --panel (chrome), plus inset top shadow on .main (box-shadow: inset 0 8px 14px -10px rgba(0,0,0,0.12)). Dusk inverts (chrome lighter than center) but keeps the framed metaphor. Likely implemented as part of shell scaffold; tracking separately so the visual property is auditable.
close_reason: Audit complete; no token changes required. All 10 themes honor the framed invariant: 8 light themes via +14.1–26.1% WCAG lum delta (panel > bg), Dusk via stronger dark-mode inset shadow (+1.2% Δ is fine since linear luminance compresses at dark ends), feminism-night via intentional inversion (dark chrome framing light canvas) per the mockup's 'Dusk inverts … keeps framed metaphor' allowance. Findings documented in design-assets/framed-luminance-audit.md with a repeatable tmp/lumcheck.cjs measurement script for future theme additions.

title: Mockup adoption — Statusbar restyle (selection count + kbd hint trail)
description:
## Goal
Restyle the existing Statusbar to match themes.html: left-side selection count, right-side keyboard hint trail with themed `<kbd>` tags.

## Owns (only this bead should modify these)
- `src/components/Statusbar.tsx`
- `src/components/Statusbar.css`

## Do NOT touch
- `src/styles/*` (tokens bead owns those — kbd styling is defined in ornaments.css)
- Any other component

## Depends on
- **mockup-tokens** (needs kbd styling from ornaments.css, `--panel`, `--rule`, `--muted`)

## Changes (themes.html:278–280, ~421–425)

1. **Container**: `background: var(--panel)`, `border-top: 1px solid var(--rule)`, 11px, `color: var(--muted)`, `padding: 0 18px`, flex with 14px gap.
2. **Left**: selection summary — e.g. `1 of 10 selected · 4.2 MB`. Pull from store state (count + total size). If nothing selected, show just `N items · totalSize`.
3. **Spacer**: `<span class="sp">` with `flex: 1`.
4. **Hints (right-aligned)**: small groups like `<kbd>⌘K</kbd> command`, `<kbd>y</kbd> yank`, `<kbd>space</kbd> preview`, `<kbd>d</kbd> drag`. Each is a span with a `<kbd>` + label.

The `<kbd>` styling comes from ornaments.css (JetBrains Mono, `var(--bg)` bg, thin border, subtle inset + drop shadow).

## Data source
Wire selection count + size from the existing store. If the drag-out mechanism is live, show a conditional "⌘-drag to export" hint when selection > 0.

## Done when
- Statusbar renders with selection count on the left and 3–4 kbd hints on the right.
- kbd tags are themed (Dawn + Dusk).
- Selection count updates as the user navigates.

## Mockup reference
`design-assets/inspirations/themes.html` — `.statusbar` CSS (line ~278), `kbd` CSS (line ~280), markup (lines ~421–425).
close_reason: Statusbar restyled to editorial tokens: panel bg + rule border, 11px muted text, .sp flex spacer. Left shows mode + 'N items · size' (or 'X of N selected · size' when marked) with tnum-oldstyle figures. Right shows kbd hint trail using ornaments.css <kbd> chips, swapping to drag/yank/paste verbs when a selection exists.

Popover persists to localStorage, shows active theme with accent ring, dismisses on outside-click / Esc. Reference: design-assets/inspirations/themes.html.

Migrated to editorial tokens (--panel/--bg/--ink/--accent/--rule/--muted/--chip) and self-hosted Fraunces/Inter Tight/JetBrains Mono. title: Motion: FLIP row reorder on sort change
description: When sortKey changes, rows currently teleport to new positions. Use FLIP technique (First-Last-Invert-Play): measure row positions before change, let React rerender, measure after, apply inverse transforms, then animate to identity with --motion-reorder. Highest 'wow' item but most complex — needs layout measurement via refs. Touches src/components/MillerColumns.tsx and FileRow.tsx.
close_reason: Deferred. FLIP row reorder needs a first-pass DOM measurement, a state swap, then delta-translate + transition-end cleanup — doable, but meaningfully larger than the other motion beads. The current sort change instantly re-renders rows; with fm-z1f's staggered fade-in already landed, a new sort doesn't feel jarring. Revisit once we add a user-testable bulk-reorder affordance where the motion would pay off.

title: Motion: context menu origin-anchored reveal
description: The .ctx-menu currently appears with no animation. Animate scale-in from 0.94→1 + fade, with transform-origin set to the cursor position (so it appears to grow from where you clicked). Use --motion-reveal. Touches src/components/FileRow.tsx (where ctx menu is rendered) and FileRow.css.
close_reason: Ctx-menu origin-anchored reveal in 960636c. showContextMenu sets transform-origin: 'left top' on the element (positioned with cursor coords, so that point IS the click). .ctx-menu runs gpPopIn → scales from 0.98→1 from the click origin. Reveal duration --dur-med / --ease-emphasis.

title: Motion: status bar message slide + auto-dismiss
description: setStatus messages currently swap in place — feels like log spam. Slide up from below with --motion-enter, auto-fade after ~3s with --motion-exit. Touches src/components/Statusbar.tsx/css and possibly store.tsx (may want timestamp on status for auto-dismiss timer).
close_reason: Status message slide + auto-dismiss in commit cd80869. Rewrote ModeLine.tsx (the actual statusMsg render target — Statusbar shows mode/summary) as stateful: mirrors store msg, bumps monotonic key on change so the animation re-runs for repeated text, auto-dismisses local display after 3s via setTimeout. Animation: gpStatusSlideIn from motion.css.

title: Motion: mark/yank/tag state transitions
description: Toggling a mark should thwack briefly with --motion-pop (spring). Yanked rows should fade to 0.55 opacity over --motion-select rather than instantly. Tag add/remove should fade. Touches src/components/FileRow.tsx/css.
close_reason: Mark/yank state transitions shipped in 5031234. .row--marked runs gpChipFlash one-shot on first mark so the accent-soft bg eases in; .row--yanked has transition on opacity/font-style via --motion-toggle so yank reads as lifted rather than a snap restyle. Shares motion.css primitives with fm-z1f/fm-9q6.

title: Motion: mode-line cross-fade on mode change
description: Current ModeLine just text-swaps between normal/find/command/visual. Cross-fade + tiny translate using --motion-toggle gives a sense of 'gearing up'. Touches src/components/ModeLine.tsx/css.
close_reason: Mode-line cross-fade in commit cd80869. Pending-keys prefix re-keys on change and runs gpPopIn (fast ease-in-out) so normal→command→find reads as 'gearing up'.

title: Motion: pathbar breadcrumb transitions
description: On navigation, breadcrumbs should slide/fade in/out rather than rerender in place. When the search input is focused, crumbs can gracefully compress to yield space. Touches src/components/Pathbar.tsx/css.
close_reason: Pathbar breadcrumb transitions in commit cd80869. Each crumb-wrap runs gpPopIn on mount (React key by index+segment so nav re-mounts). Crumbs yield width to search on :focus-within via opacity + max-width transition so they don't clip mid-crumb.
